history.heading: Land of many waters
paragraphs: Guyana, on the northeast coast of South America, takes its name from an indigenous word meaning "land of many waters". It was home to Arawak, Carib, Warao and other indigenous peoples. The Dutch established colonies in the 17th century and developed sugar plantations worked by enslaved Africans. A major slave revolt in Berbice in 1763, led by Cuffy, is commemorated as a national event.

Britain took control during the Napoleonic Wars and united the colonies as British Guiana in 1831. After slavery was abolished in 1834, about 240,000 indentured labourers were brought from India, as well as smaller numbers from Portugal (Madeira) and China.

history.heading: Independence
paragraphs: British Guiana became independent on 26 May 1966 as Guyana, and a republic in 1970. Politics became divided along ethnic lines between the People's Progressive Party, supported mainly by Indo-Guyanese and led by Cheddi Jagan, and the People's National Congress, supported mainly by Afro-Guyanese and led by Forbes Burnham, who ruled from 1964 to 1985.

In 1978 over 900 members of the American cult Peoples Temple died in a mass murder-suicide at Jonestown. In 2015 ExxonMobil discovered large offshore oil reserves, transforming the country's prospects.

culture.heading: A Caribbean nation in South America
paragraphs: Guyana is the only English-speaking country in South America, and culturally it identifies with the Caribbean. Guyanese Creole is widely spoken. The population is mainly of Indian and African descent, with mixed, indigenous, Chinese and Portuguese minorities. Christianity, Hinduism and Islam are all practised, and Diwali, Phagwah (Holi) and Eid are national holidays.
Pepperpot, a meat stew flavoured with cassareep from cassava, is the national dish. Cricket is very popular. Kaieteur Falls is one of the world's most powerful single-drop waterfalls.

politics.heading: Republic
paragraphs: Guyana is a republic in which the president, the leader of the party winning the most votes in parliamentary elections, is head of state and government. Ethnic polarisation shapes elections. The People's Progressive Party/Civic has governed since 2020 and won again in 2025.
Venezuela claims about two-thirds of Guyana's territory, the Essequibo region, west of the Essequibo River; tensions rose sharply in 2023, and the case is before the International Court of Justice.

economy.heading: Oil boom
paragraphs: Since oil production began in 2019, Guyana has had one of the fastest-growing economies in the world, with growth rates often above 30 percent. Oil now dominates exports, and a sovereign wealth fund manages revenues. The government is investing heavily in roads, housing, a gas-to-energy project and services.

Before oil, the economy relied on gold, bauxite, sugar, rice, timber and shrimp. Challenges include avoiding the "resource curse", sharing wealth fairly and environmental risks. The currency is the Guyanese dollar.
